engagement_title: Marisol Cove shoulder season campaign: the page, the booking brochure, the social set, and the printed rate cards the agents hand over
vertical: Food, hospitality and travel. A fourteen room boutique clifftop hotel above a cove on the Mendocino coast, Northern California, pushing its autumn and winter shoulder season across its own page, a booking agent brochure, a social set and a printed per room rate card run.
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, a premium hospitality client asking for luxury style website hero banners with a clean, premium, modern design and, in the client's own words, the 'ability to maintain consistent brand identity across all creative assets'. The post names no property, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional hotel Marisol Cove. Only the sourcing platform is named, as provenance; the stock library, the booking agents and the printer are all generic, and no real hotel, person, agency, marketplace, software or trademark appears anywhere. The ledger's STRENGTHEN verdict keeps the concept (one campaign, one look, several destinations, everything editable) and deepens it to the current standard, because CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is. HTML authoring now returns a native editable Express document carrying mixed canvas sizes in one export, a mark photographed on a painted sign can be recovered as real vector, and a printer's press PDF plus a rates spreadsheet is a genuine one record per page merge. So the real job this client needed was never three hero banners: it was the campaign, the print run their booking agents actually hand over, and files they can keep editing without re-commissioning anyone.
client_one_liner: Our shoulder season push has to run off licensed coastal pictures brought to the light we actually have here, our lost mark has to come back off a photograph of the entrance sign, and our agents need nine printed rate cards, all of it editable by us afterwards.
client_brief:
Marisol Cove, autumn and winter push

We are a fourteen room hotel on the bluff above a cove on the Mendocino coast. Two owners, nine staff. Rooms run three hundred and forty to six hundred and twenty dollars a night. Our guests are couples and small groups, thirty to fifty five, and they come for the path down to the beach and for the dining room. There is no pool and there is no spa.

Autumn and winter are our thin months and this is the first year we are pushing them properly. Everything a guest sees changes at once: the page we send people to, the brochure our booking agents hand across a desk, and the set we post.

Where we actually are. There has been no photographer's shoot. What exists is our own room photographs, taken on two phones over two years, plus whatever we license from the stock library. Our office manager went through the thumbnails and shortlisted some coastal frames she likes. All of it has to end up looking like one place under one light: warm but never orange, quiet, the light we get here about an hour before sunset.

Our mark is a small wordmark with a wave rule under it. The file went with the designer who drew it in 2019. What we still have is a photograph of the painted sign at the entrance. We need the mark back as artwork we can place at any size on any colour.

We also need the rate cards, one card per room type, printed, for the fourteen travel agents who sell us. Our printer still had last season's card and sent the file over. The rates and what each room includes are in the spreadsheet.

The page, the brochure and the social set have to stay editable by us, because the featured room and the dates move every few weeks.

Finally a note: what you did, what type we are on, what the stock costs us, and anything about the mark or the printing we should know.
price_band_and_audience: Boutique premium coastal rooms at 340 to 620 dollars a night, guests 30 to 55, couples and small groups, experience led rather than amenity led. The band is load bearing. At this rate the campaign runs on serene full bleed photography, generous air, a small quiet mark and rates set in a plain table that the guest reads once and trusts. Push it down into a discount travel look (burst badges, stacked savings callouts, three deals a screen, a dense grid of small pictures) and the same rooms read as a 120 dollar highway motel, which repels the guest who was going to book and permanently anchors the rate lower. Push it up into black ground, foil serif, eight words a page luxury and it reads as a 1,400 dollar a night private estate, which misprices the property and reads as dishonest the moment the guest arrives at a fourteen room hotel with no spa. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: The quiet side of the coast.
brand_identity.sector: A fourteen room boutique hotel on the bluff above a cove, selling nights and the dining room to couples and small groups.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2014, on the Mendocino coast of Northern California, run by two owners with nine staff.
brand_identity.about: Marisol Cove is a small clifftop hotel built around a path down to a private beach and a dining room people plan a trip for. There is no pool and no spa, and the point of the place is the light, the water and being left alone. The autumn and winter shoulder season is the first the owners are pushing properly.
brand_identity.audience: Couples and small groups aged 30 to 55, experience led rather than amenity led, who book for the setting and the food and return in the quiet months.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Rooms run 340 to 620 dollars a night. Boutique premium, above a coastal inn and well below a resort or private estate. The rate is carried by the setting, not by facilities.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet high contrast serif for display, set large and given air, paired with a plain humanist sans for rates, captions and body. Coastal premium, never resort brochure and never luxury estate. Generous leading, restrained sizes.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, plain and specific. It describes what is actually there and lets the reader picture it. Example line the brand would write: An hour before sunset the light comes off the water and the whole cove goes gold. That is when to walk down.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The logo file was lost with the designer who drew it in 2019. The mark, a small caps wordmark over a hairline wave rule, survives only as the painted sign at the entrance, which the owners have photographed. Room photography is the owners' own phone frames plus licensed stock. No usable brand files remain beyond the sign photo.
brand_identity.values: One place under one light. Every guest facing piece should read as the same specific cove, honest about a fourteen room hotel rather than dressed up as something grander.

assets_supplied.name: marisol_room_photos/ (11 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: The owners' own photographs of rooms, the terrace, the path down to the cove and two dining room corners, taken on two phones across two years.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Ours, from two phones over a couple of years. Not professional, but they are the rooms as they actually are."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Seven are camera scale, but three are already-cropped web exports around a thousand pixels on the long edge and cannot reach the brochure picture box without interpolation, which the crop tool performs up to a two times cap while reporting it only inside its own tradeoffs object. Two frames are the same room shot from opposite corners and are filed under two different room names, which no filename reveals.

assets_supplied.name: marisol_stock_shortlist.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The office manager's shortlist of coastal frames from the stock library, recorded as keywords and thumbnail impressions.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The ones I liked. The cove one at dusk especially."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A shortlist made from 240 pixel thumbnails. A frame's true colour and true crop only exist after the full resolution download, and the dusk frame she likes best is a cold blue grey at full size that will not come to the house warmth without the sand going muddy. One other shortlisted frame is generative-tech, which the property's insurer forbids in booking material, and that flag is exposed only in the search response and never on the thumbnail.

assets_supplied.name: marisol_sign_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the painted entrance sign: a small-caps wordmark in one deep ink over a hairline wave rule, on a weathered pale board.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the mark still lives. The designer's drive went in 2019."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Disjoint painted lettering on a photographed substrate. A prompt naming the sign returns the board rather than the paint, background removal on disjoint lettering keeps two or three letters and drops the rest while reporting success, and the trace comes back with no viewBox and an opaque full canvas rectangle at path zero. The paint and the weathered board also run close in value across the sunlit left third.

assets_supplied.name: marisol_rate_card_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last season's single rate card exactly as the printer supplied it: a real press PDF with embedded font subsets, one card per page.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What our printer prints from. The layout is fine, only the rooms and the numbers change."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card reads as six separate typographic blocks but is set as one continuous flow, so what the conversion exposes as mappable frames is nothing like the printed page suggests. Worse, the structure readout drops one run from the contact block while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past it is short by exactly that run, and the validator still answers VALID.

assets_supplied.name: marisol_rates_autumn.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Ten rows: room name, sleeps, shoulder rate, winter rate, minimum stay, and an Includes line per room.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The nine rooms with the new rates. The Includes wording came from the front desk."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Ten rows for nine room types: the Boathouse Loft appears twice, once as The Boathouse, with identical rates. Separately the Cypress Suite's Includes line is roughly three times the length of the others, and in a fixed frame at trim the overflow does not spill anywhere visible, it simply stops rendering partway through a word.

assets_supplied.name: marisol_copy.md
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the amenity list, the dining room note, the cancellation line and the seasonal paragraph the owners want on the page and in the brochure.

acceptance_bar: The licensed frames, the owners' room photographs and every picture in the campaign read as one place under one light when they sit next to each other: one white point, one warmth, one black point. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no crop or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry. A picture that reaches its box by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable at page scale.
No generative-tech stock frame appears anywhere in the delivered campaign, and every licensed frame is accounted for in the note with what it cost.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, and it still reads as the mark at the size it actually reproduces in the page header over the photograph, and reversed on colour.

The rate card run is one press PDF whose page count equals the true room type count after the spreadsheet is reconciled, in the room order the owners use, with every field present on every page and nothing stopping mid word at the frame edge.
Every room type has its own card and no card stands in for two rooms.

The campaign is ONE native editable Express document carrying every canvas in its own size (the page, the brochure pages, each social size, the basis canvas), delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
Every photograph in that document is embedded image data rather than a reference, and no canvas shows an empty grey box where a picture should be.
Headline copy sits legibly over the photography on every canvas, not only the first one, and the rate table is a real table with its own cells rather than a picture of a table.
One type system across every canvas and the printed cards, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual numeric weight used.

The note states what was applied per photograph and why any frame differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, the room reconciliation, the stock licensing position, and anything about the mark or the print run the owners should know.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision in the commission. It fixes one house target off the strongest frame and brings the licensed coastal frames and the owners' phone photographs toward it one call at a time, applies confined corrections where a whole frame move takes the water green or the sand grey, cuts each picture to the box it fills without ever enlarging, and recovers the wordmark at paint level off a photographed sign with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole campaign as one native editable document carrying the page, the brochure pages at true millimetre size, three social canvases and the basis canvas, each declaring its own canvas. This is the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the mark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, the rate table goes in as a real table, and family and weight are declared on every text element.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: One type system for the page, the brochure, the social set and the printed cards. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on quiet coastal premium rather than either resort brochure or luxury estate. Numeric weights are non-standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name has to be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the coastal photography the property does not own, IP clean and at genuine camera scale, with generative-tech candidates excluded on the flag rather than by eye and with the office manager's thumbnail shortlist treated as a starting point rather than a decision. The Boards half persists the selects set the two owners sign off from, placed within the twelve per call cap, with a partial success read as partial.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (inventory and validator modes), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange, outputSpecs), document_render_layout (resolution, createSeparateFiles)
adobe_surfaces.role: The agent rate card run, built backwards out of the printer's own press PDF because no native template exists. It converts the card, exports the IDML to see what the document actually contains rather than what the printed page suggests, reconciles the spreadsheet against the real room list, builds and verifies a live merge template, then delivers one press PDF at one record per page plus per record proofs rendered at true print resolution for the owners to sign off.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The page, brochure and social set are one authored fixed canvas document because the owners edit them every few weeks. The rate cards are a record per page print run and belong on the merge surface. Nothing here is ambiguous, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, plus the fact that the image tools enforce their own domain whitelist, so nothing reaches them except through this route or a licensed stock URL.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all eleven room photographs and the sign photograph and triage them: which are camera scale and which are already-cropped web exports, which are level, which sit under which light, and what each frame actually shows.
trajectory.judgement: The owners describe eleven room photographs. Only the pictures can settle whether that is eleven different rooms, and reading them against the room list is slower than counting files and is not the same thing.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering scale, tilt, illuminant and subject identity.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Search the coastal subjects with short generic queries, filter to photography, read the generative-tech flag on every candidate, then license and download the chosen frames at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: The shortlist is a starting point, not a decision. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used, and the insurer's rule is enforced from the returned flag rather than from how a thumbnail looks.
trajectory.produces: Licensed, IP clean, camera scale coastal frames with their cost and their flags recorded.

trajectory.action: Fix one house target off the strongest frame and bring each licensed frame and each usable room photograph toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a campaign, not a set of good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for two phones, two years and a stock library. The agent holds one destination and reaches it by different routes.
trajectory.produces: A graded house set at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confined corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong, selecting materials by their own visual properties rather than by the object they belong to.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate. Bringing warmth into a frame globally takes the water toward green and the white bed linen toward cream, and those are the two things a guest reads first.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have broken the water or the linen.

trajectory.action: Cut every picture to the box it actually fills on its destination canvas, reading the tradeoffs each call returns rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoffs array is the only channel that reports an enlargement, and it carries no warning language. A web export that will not reach the brochure box is a frame to reassign or to name, not one to interpolate.
trajectory.produces: Destination sized pictures with their returned tradeoffs recorded per frame.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark off the sign: a paint level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas path removed. Produce a single colour mark and a colour accurate variant.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the paint and not the board, which polarity to trace, and which variant is the deliverable. Background removal is the wrong instrument on disjoint painted lettering.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a 340 to 620 dollar room and a guest who is choosing between three coastal hotels. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's rate card PDF, export the IDML, and read the real frame inventory: how many text frames, what bounds, what applied type, what graphic frames exist.
trajectory.judgement: Frame granularity from a PDF is not under the agent's control, and the printed card's visual blocks are no evidence of it. Nothing can be promised about mapping until the document itself has been looked at.
trajectory.produces: A true frame inventory of the converted card, written down before any mapping is drafted.

trajectory.action: Reconcile the spreadsheet against the owners' room list, then build the field mapping against the document's true story text, validate it, prepare the merge template, and re-export the IDML to confirm every placeholder is actually present.
trajectory.judgement: Ten rows and nine rooms cannot both be right, and the reconciliation is the agent's call to make and to report. The validator answering VALID and the prepare step answering success are not evidence that a placeholder landed; only the round tripped document is.
trajectory.produces: A live merge template whose placeholders have been confirmed by inspection, plus a written room reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Merge to one press PDF at one record per page, merge again to the native format, then render per record proofs at true print resolution, and read every merged page.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equal to room count is the cheap check. Reading the pages is the real one, because a field that never landed and a line that stopped rendering both come back as a successful merge.
trajectory.produces: One press PDF for the printer, per record proofs for the owners, and a read of every page.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying every canvas as its own root at its own declared size, inline every photograph as image data, place the mark as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized left and top anchored wrapper, set the rate table as a real table, declare family and weight on every text element, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how much air the page carries and how quietly the rates sit.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole campaign, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every canvas after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board and add the graded house set and the licensed frames within the per call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and the vector mark is not boardable, so it belongs in the note instead.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Write the note: per photograph what was applied and why, every resize any tool reported, the room reconciliation, the stock licensing position and cost, the type system by role, and what the owners should know about the mark and about the print run.
trajectory.judgement: The note is the deliverable that survives the season. It has to be specific enough that the next freelancer does not repeat the archaeology, and honest about anything that could not be delivered.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the licensed coastal frames actually are, once they are full size and sitting beside the graded set. Everything available before licensing is a 240 pixel thumbnail, which carries neither the frame's true cast nor its usable crop, and the owners' shortlist was made from exactly those thumbnails. The dusk frame the office manager likes best comes down as a cold blue grey whose warmth cannot be reached without the sand going muddy and the water going flat, and that verdict exists only in the adjacency: on its own it is a good photograph, and next to the graded room set it is a different day in a different place.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because full resolution colour does not exist until the frame is licensed and downloaded, and no parameter reveals it earlier. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the office manager shortlisted frames she likes and that everything must end up looking like one place. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different search and a fresh licensing decision with a real cost attached, or a reassignment of that frame to a canvas where its cast reads as intentional.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-search the coastal subjects with different short queries, read the generative-tech flag on every new candidate, license a replacement, grade it into the house target, and re-judge it beside the set rather than on its own. Then re-cut whichever canvases had been built around the rejected frame.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A campaign whose page, brochure and social set are visibly three different coastal places, on a property whose entire pitch is that it is one specific cove, with a cold dusk hero anchoring the most expensive canvas.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the merged rate cards actually say. The printed card reads as six separate typographic blocks, but what the conversion exposes as mappable frames is not under the agent's control and can collapse to a single continuous flow, which changes the entire mapping strategy. On top of that, the structure readout of that flow drops one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed, every offset after it is short by exactly that run, the validator answers VALID with no warnings, and the prepare step answers success. Two fields then never land on any card. In the same pass, the one Includes line that is three times longer than its neighbours does not spill anywhere visible at trim, it simply stops rendering partway through a word.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and no parameter controls it: granularity is a property of the source PDF, and both the validator and the prepare step report success on offsets computed from an incomplete readout. (b) Nothing states it: the owners say the layout is fine and only the rooms and the numbers change. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different mapping strategy computed from the document's true story text plus a copy decision on the record that will not fit.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the exported document rather than from the readout, recompute every offset against it, rebuild and re-verify the template by round tripping the document and confirming each placeholder is present, re-merge, and re-read every page. Then resolve the long Includes line by shortening it with the owners' wording rather than letting it stop mid word, and record that decision.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Nine printed cards handed to fourteen travel agents with the rate line and the season line silently missing from every one of them, and one room's inclusions ending mid word, after a merge that reported success at every stage.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark still reads as the mark at the size it actually reproduces, on the ground it actually sits on. The trace looks clean and complete at canvas size on white. In the page header it is small and it sits over a full bleed photograph, and at that size the wave rule can thin to nothing and the tight counters in the small-caps letterforms can close, so the wordmark reads as a dark smudge with the right silhouette. Which of those happens depends on the paint edge in that particular photograph of that particular weathered sign, and it is visible only after the canvas is exported and looked at at reproduction size.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that avoids it and no measurement available: the connector has no ruler and no way to inspect a rendered glyph, so the only evidence is the exported canvas itself. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for artwork placeable at any size on any colour, which is the client's standing requirement, not a warning that this trace will fail small. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different raster preparation upstream, a tighter paint level selection or the opposite polarity or a bounds crop before tracing, and possibly a different variant carrying the header entirely.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare the mark from the sign photograph through a different selection and polarity, re-trace, re-apply the viewBox and strip the opaque path again, decide whether the single colour or the colour accurate variant carries the header, re-author the canvas around whichever it is, re-run the readiness check and re-export.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A campaign whose header carries a smudge where the hotel's only surviving mark should be, delivered as an editable document that reported success throughout, with the owners told their mark had been recovered.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which need an authored fixed canvas document, and which are a record per page print run, given that only one surface here composes free form layout and only one produces a per record print file.
Whether the office manager's thumbnail shortlist survives contact with the full resolution frames, and what it costs to replace one that does not.
How the insurer's rule against generative imagery is actually enforced, given the flag exists in the search response and not on the thumbnail.
How far to push the two phone camera years toward one light before a frame stops being worth saving, versus naming it in the note.
Which of the owners' web export frames can carry a brochure picture box at all, and what to do with the ones that cannot, given that interpolation is available and silent.

Selection prompt wording on the sign: naming the sign takes the board, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the mark, and background removal on disjoint lettering is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which mark variant carries the page header, judged at reproduction size over the photograph rather than at full canvas.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a boutique coastal band and a guest comparing three hotels, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Whether ten spreadsheet rows and nine room types is a data error or a room the owners sell twice, and how to say so.
What to do with the one Includes line that will not fit the card frame, given the client's wording is the client's and the overflow is invisible.
How much air the campaign carries. At this band restraint is the design, and a dense, deal led page is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of a coastal hotel. IDENTITY: these are this property's actual rooms, its actual cove and its actual painted sign, and the mark must be RECOVERED off that sign rather than reinvented, because a regenerated wordmark is a different hotel's logo. SPEC: the rate cards are a real print run whose page count must equal the room count, whose fields must all land, and whose artwork is the printer's own; the stock must be genuinely licensed and demonstrably not generative, because the insurer's rule attaches to the licence and not to the look. EDITABILITY: the campaign is defined by being editable, since the featured room and the dates move every few weeks and two owners with nine staff cannot re-commission a designer each time. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this licensed frame actually sit with the graded set, did every field land on every card, does the recovered mark still read at header size over a photograph.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and upscale_factor, fill_area, remove_background and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls, and the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the disjoint lettering collapse of remove_background, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero are live findings that the acceptance bar scores. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, isGenTech exposed in the search response, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, renditionURL confirmed as a 240 pixel thumbnail only, and boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. INDESIGN: the whole chain is verified end to end, convert_pdf_to_indd on a real font embedding PDF, export_idml as the structure inspection channel, generate_indd_mapping_prompt in both inventory and validator modes, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with page count equal to row count for PDF output, and document_render_layout at 300 DPI with createSeparateFiles in verified correct order. The merge checkpoint rests on documented findings rather than assumptions: frame granularity from a PDF collapsed a six line flow to ONE TextFrame with zero graphic frames, and textContent dropped a 17 character run while keeping its line break so the validator returned VALID and only 3 of 5 mappings landed. Multi record raster order is known bad, so per record proofs go through createSeparateFiles, not through raster outputSpecs. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, mm canvases resolve exactly, tables and inline SVG become native editable objects, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. Photos are base64 inlined because every external URL resolved to a placeholder, and transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed claim from a PDF derived template, no pdfPreset, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text-to-image, no generative expand, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
